- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >2%, model frequently fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to 10-day average or 15% below prior high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior, 30% sentiment) to dampen volatility.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the high side; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for each negative sentiment day in the 3-day window.
- If 3+ consecutive sentiment values are negative, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; apply 10-day moving average as baseline and adjust forecast by ±1–2% based on sentiment trend direction.
